owner_decision: On 2026-11-06 the owner accepted declared hypotheses for unobserved geometry, provided each one is tagged, shown in a distinct colour and never claimed as measured.
rule: Nothing in this register is a measurement. A hypothesis is retired only by the evidence named in 'retire_with'. The scorecard's twin->scan 'inferred' area is the geometric footprint of these entries.

items.region: fin roots and the deep floor of every fin gap
items.how: winding-number 0.5 iso-surface of the open scan; the scanner never saw these surfaces (the 87 boundary loops of 20 mm or more hold 67% of open edges, mostly here)
items.retire_with: CT of the specimen, a rescan with fin-gap coverage, or a supplier drawing of the fin roots

searched_on_2026_11_22.what: no published fin pitch, fin thickness, root radius or gap-floor shape of a 911, 930, 935 or Xtreme head was found; the closure is kept and the request stays open. The class that holds these regions is 13.6% of the v2 body's area (75% of its inferred area), together with the rest of the outer closure

items.region: four head-stud through passages parallel to the bore axis
items.how: interior walls are mostly unobserved; v0 keeps the winding-number closure; v1 replaces it with straight analytic bores fitted on the observed deck notches and cam-side openings
items.retire_with: measured passage diameter and axis at both ends on the specimen or a drawing

fitted_on_2026_11_11.what: four passages fitted on their acquired walls: diameter 10.50 to 10.96 mm, two of the four determined by the fit, none confirmed by the CloudCompare check (63% to 87% of held-out vertices within 0.2 mm). The unobserved middle of each passage is still closure
fitted_on_2026_11_11.claim: fitted numbers on scan data whose scale is an owner instruction; not a dimension of the specimen and not evidence that retires this hypothesis

items.region: threaded holes under the 10 removed studs (6 cam-side, 2 per flange)
items.how: studs are hardware and are removed; their seats are capped by the closure. A tapped hole (thread class, depth) is not observable from the surface
items.retire_with: stud specification and tapped-hole depth from a drawing or measurement

items.region: intake and exhaust port walls beyond the depth the scanner reached, valve-guide bosses inside the ports
items.how: winding-number closure; v1 lofts the ports through observed cross-sections only and marks the interpolated span
items.retire_with: port moulds, CT, or a borescope survey with registered sections

searched_on_2026_11_22.what: no published port diameter, shape, bowl, throat, short-side radius, guide boss or port volume of a 935 or Xtreme head was found, and no captioned cutaway; the maker states that it digitises and machines its ports, but publishes no geometry. In the v2 body the port voids hold 2.2% of the body's area as inferred closure (12% of the inferred area); that closure is kept

declared_rule_on_2026_11_22.what: in the port domain only, the closure beyond the last scan section is replaced by the declared rule H17; the v2 body keeps the closure

items.region: valve seat inserts, guide bores and their interference fits
items.how: valve, seat insert and guide of each valve are separate solids of revolution on the fitted axes (params/valve-seat-guide.json), every value from params/valve-seat-guide-case.json: published values of other heads and the maker's catalogue ranges (H16), fits on the scan, and explicit assumptions where nothing was found (insert height, valve margin and tulip, stem clearance). The v2 body still holds the scanned guides and seats as one solid; no interference fit is modelled
items.retire_with: supplier valvetrain specification for this head variant

modelled_on_2026_11_22.what: bodies built and checked: no overlap closed or at the published largest lifts, stems run in the guides, the two heads stay 0.59 mm apart with both at their largest lift. The inlet contact band lies inside the fitted seat window; the exhaust band reaches 0.09 mm (radius) inside its inner edge
modelled_on_2026_11_22.why_not_retired: the maker publishes ranges for families of heads, not the specification of this head; no part of the specimen was measured

fitted_on_2026_11_11.what: guide bores, guide outside diameters, throats, seats and spring seats fitted where the scanner reached them: guide bore 8.51 mm seen over 48.8 mm on valve_y_minus, seats near 45 and 49 degrees, valve axes 25.9 and 29.9 degrees from the bore axis. Of these fits CloudCompare confirms the valve_y_plus throat and seat only. Nothing is modelled in a body: the status stays as it was, and inserts, materials, interference fits and the valves themselves remain unknown
fitted_on_2026_11_11.claim: fitted numbers on scan data whose scale is an owner instruction; not a dimension of the specimen and not evidence that retires this hypothesis

items.how: observed bore openings are kept as scanned; thread form and depth are not modelled

fitted_on_2026_11_11.what: both thread bores fitted as scanned: 11.49 and 11.28 mm, 29.2 and 28.6 degrees from the bore axis, with a chamber-side relief of 14.3 mm and a well of about 25 mm. Neither bore is confirmed by the CloudCompare check; both seat faces are. Thread form, pitch and reach are not observable at this scan pitch
fitted_on_2026_11_11.claim: fitted numbers on scan data whose scale is an owner instruction; not a dimension of the specimen and not evidence that retires this hypothesis

items.region: any oil or breather passage not open to the scanned surface
items.how: none is invented; the twin contains no internal gallery

searched_on_2026_11_22.what: a Porsche patent (US 4941436 A, priority 1988) describes oil led through bores of an air-cooled head, perpendicular to the cam-housing joint, to a cooling ring around the exhaust valve seat; a seller describes 935 heads with oil-cooled exhaust guides (recorded 2026-10-28; its page refused automated readers on 2026-11-22). Neither shows that this head has a gallery, nor where; none is modelled and the request stays open

items.region: 4 mm inclined rod-like protrusion on the cam side (about x=-19, y=-88)
items.how: it does not pass the stud test (axis inclined 36 degrees to the bore axis, protrudes 10 mm), so it is kept as head body and flagged
items.retire_with: photograph or drawing identifying the feature

searched_on_2026_11_22.what: no source describes a pin, rod or tube of about 4 mm standing out of the cam-side face of a 911, 930, 935 or Xtreme head; the nearest published features (the head temperature sensor of the 993, the oil bores of US 4941436 A) give neither this diameter nor this angle. The feature stays unclassified

items.region: which valve is the inlet and which the exhaust
items.how: valve_y_minus is taken as the inlet and valve_y_plus as the exhaust. Three published relations of other heads point the same way and none against: the larger seat and throat (48.97 and 45.81 mm against 43.10 and 38.47 mm) match the larger inlet valve of the production 930 Turbo (49 against 41.5 mm) and of both maker catalogue families whose ranges do not overlap; the valve angles (25.89 and 29.89 degrees) match the published inlet and exhaust angles of the 964 Turbo 3.3 (25.5 and 30.25), the other way round would miss by 4.4 degrees; and the larger flange opening (41.8 against 40.5 mm equivalent diameter) matches a 935 head set listed with 41 mm intake and 40 mm exhaust ports. None of these describes this head
items.retire_with: supplier documentation of this head, or an inspection of the ports and valves of the specimen

items.region: two closed valves, two guides and two spark plugs in the assembly thermal screen
items.how: solids of revolution about the fitted axes: valve heads on the fitted seat cones, stems filling the fitted guide bores, guides as tubes of the fitted outside diameter, plugs filling the thread bores; every other length comes from params/assembly-case.json. They exist only in the united thermal domain, not in the CAD body, the USD stages or the 3MF
items.retire_with: valve, guide and plug drawings or the parts themselves
items.kept_on_2026_11_22: the two thermal screens ran on these solids and were not rerun, so their records still rest on them. The separate valve, seat insert and guide bodies of params/valve-seat-guide.json (H16) are the ones to use for any new screen; neither set is a drawing or a part, so the retiring evidence has not arrived

items.region: conductivities of valve, guide and plug; contact at seats, guides, threads and the cylinder joint
items.how: valve steel 20, bronze guide 60 and plug steel 45 W/(m K); seat inserts keep the head alloy's conductivity; every contact is perfect, with no gap and no contact resistance
items.retire_with: material specifications of the fitted parts and a contact conductance from test or literature for each joint

items.region: gas, port, air and cylinder boundary conditions of the assembly thermal screen
items.how: six films with one sink temperature and one coefficient each, and four variants of them (params/assembly-case.json): two declared, two with the gas side scaled to published generic wall loadings; the cylinder is a contact condition in the register recess at one temperature, not a modelled part; oil only as a film on the spring pockets; no radiation, both valves closed
items.retire_with: an engine heat balance and measured head temperatures for one operating point

items.region: the cylinder barrel under the head in the heat-path case of the assembly thermal screen
items.how: a tube on the bore axis: bore on the fitted chamber shoulder (92.80 mm), collar filling the fitted register recess, heights and lower register from the MAHLE replacement cylinder 503 WR 44 00 of the 993 Turbo (total 114.5 mm, collar 77.27 mm, register 107.0 mm), which is another engine; conductivity 150 W/(m K) in 95 to 191, fins as one effective film of 3 (1.5 to 6) times the air film, gas at NACA Report 612's 316 °C on the whole bore, a crankcase contact at the oil temperature below the shoulder (params/assembly-heat-paths-case.json)
items.retire_with: a drawing or a scan of the barrel used with this head, its alloy, and its fin geometry

items.region: the faces oil reaches in the heat-path case: spring pockets, guide tops and stems, and the cam-housing face
items.how: oil film of the first case (500 W/(m2 K), swept 100 to 2000) extended to the walls and mouth of each spring pocket; every face at or above the fitted cam face (z 85.87 mm, 2 mm band), outside the pockets and plug wells, takes one lumped coefficient of 1000 (300 to 3000) W/(m2 K) to the oil temperature, 90 °C (80 to 100, published for other 911 engines)
items.retire_with: the cam housing and its gasket line for this head, and an oil temperature and heat flow measured at one operating point

items.region: contact conductance at the valve seats, valve stems, guides, plug threads and seats, and the barrel collar in the register recess
items.how: no published number was found for any joint (params/thermal-literature-bounds.json); each takes 10,000 W/(m2 K), swept from 1,000 to 100,000. The meshed interface of each joint is scaled to the area it projects onto the part surface (about 0.6 of the meshed area)
items.retire_with: a contact conductance from test or literature for each joint, with its contact pressure and surface finish

items.region: dimensions, angles, lifts and materials of the valves, seat inserts and guides of both valves
items.how: published values of other heads (production 930 Turbo and 911 parts, a valve maker's 8 mm-stem 911 valves, a workshop's 911 seat and guide practice) and the ranges of the head maker's catalogue, each with its source in params/valve-seat-guide-case.json; where nothing was found the value is an explicit assumption with a range: seat-insert height (7 mm), inlet insert outside diameter (derived from the exhaust ring), valve margin, face and tulip, stem clearance (0.05 mm). Valve heads 49 and 41.5 mm, the only sizes common to the two catalogue families a 935 head could belong to
items.retire_with: the supplier's valvetrain specification of this head, or the valves, seats and guides of the specimen measured

items.region: each port between its last closed scan section and the fitted valve throat: the bend, the bowl and the guide boss in it
items.how: the convex hull of the last scan section, with the guide boss taken out of its outline, and the fitted throat circle at the top of the throat window; the fitted guide cylinder is cut from it (source/port_domain.py, params/port-domain.json). The rule adds no port dimension of its own; its only setting is the 1 mm margin that picks the rays ending on the guide boss. It lives in the port domain only, not in the v2 body
items.retire_with: registered sections of the port bend and bowl from CT, moulds or a borescope survey (the evidence that retires H04)

items.region: the whole specimen: maker, process, head type, valve stems and spark-plug thread
items.status: assumed by owner decision 2026-11-22, not confirmed
items.how: the scanned head is taken to be a new aftermarket casting by Xtreme Cylinder Heads, cast then machined (the seller's private statement of 2026-10-11, recorded in the repository; the listing's 'billet' is superseded), made for a Porsche 935: one air-cooled two-valve head per cylinder with two spark plugs and four head-stud passages. From the maker's published options it takes 8 mm valve stems and the 12 mm plug, read as M12 x 1.25 (ISO 28741). Candidates, evidence for and against, and the questions for the reviewer: params/specimen-identity.json
items.retire_with: the maker's or the seller's statement naming the product, program and casting, or a part number, casting mark or engraved logo legible on the specimen

items.region: cylinder bore and chamber edge: the engine and the maker's program the head serves
items.status: assumed by owner decision 2026-11-22, not confirmed
items.how: the head is taken to belong to the maker's 2.0 - 2.9 liter program and to the 2.85 L 935 engine, whose bore is at most 92.8 mm with the 70.4 mm stroke under the 4.0 L class and the 1.4 turbo factor (published bores disagree: 92.0, 92.4 and 92.8 mm); the fitted chamber shoulder, 92.80 mm, is taken to be the bore. The choice rests partly on that fit under the 1 mm unit, so the shoulder is not counted as a check of the unit (params/scale-check.json). The maker's 3.0 - 3.5 liter program, for bores of 95 mm and more, stays a live alternative
items.retire_with: the maker's or the seller's statement of the program and bore, the chamber volume as cc'd on the specimen, or a contributed measurement of the chamber edge and of the cylinder used with it
